forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Cheltenham council to fall £563,000 short of minimum reserves by March
news_drafts.lead: Cheltenham's general reserves are forecast to fall to £937,000 by 31 March 2027, leaving the council £563,000 below the level its Section 151 Officer, the chief finance officer, assesses as prudent. An £838,000 forecast overspend is the cause. At the same time, the council's capital programme — money spent on long-lived assets such as buildings — is being cut by 13.5%, from £42.96m to £37.1m. The National Cyber Innovation Centre at Golden Valley, budgeted at £32.85m, is unaffected and now represents 89 per cent of the entire capital spending plan. Separately, the Housing Revenue Account, which manages council housing and is funded by rents, is forecast to overspend by £650,000, driven by £465,000 in lost rental income from vacant properties and £201,000 in additional borrowing costs from higher interest rates.

findings.committee: Joint Scrutiny Panel - Local Government Reorganisation
findings.headline: Full costs of operating under a shadow authority model have not yet been quantified.
findings.detail: The paper says these costs may create additional pressures in governance, democratic services, member support and ICT. Appendix B shows Shadow Election Costs of £1,500,000, while section 6 refers to a dedicated £600k provision for election costs.
findings.matters: An unquantified shadow authority cost is an open liability for every council in the programme, and the two election figures in the paper are not reconciled in the text.
findings.figures: £600k election provision (section 6); Shadow Election Costs £1,500,000 (Appendix B); Shadow Chief Executive / Member Costs £311,100
findings.quote: However, the full costs associated with operating under a shadow authority model have not yet been quantified

findings.committee: Joint Scrutiny Panel - Local Government Reorganisation
findings.headline: Partner contributions of £2.463 million received from five councils; Gloucester City Council's contribution is deferred under the agreed profile.
findings.detail: Actual expenditure to 30 September 2026 was £719k, up from £564k at period 5. The paper notes that recharges from Cotswolds DC, Stroud BC and Tewkesbury BC are still outstanding, with POs issued in September. The contributions figure is unchanged since period 5, and the paper states that the scheduled October invoicing round is paused as a cashflow measure.
findings.matters: Contributions received well exceed expenditure to date, so cash position and invoicing timing are the relevant points for a finance director or lender.
findings.figures: £2.463 million contributions received (£2,462,815 in Appendix A); actual expenditure £719k (£564k at period 5); total budget £22.2 million
findings.quote: Contributions of £2.463 million have been received by Gloucestershire County Council from five district and borough councils, this has not changed since period 5.

findings.committee: Joint Scrutiny Panel - Local Government Reorganisation
findings.headline: £900k MHCLG Section 31 grant is included in the £22.2 million total budget but has not yet been received.
findings.detail: The grant was added to the original £21.3 million implementation budget when the revised budget was set. The paper does not give a receipt date.
findings.matters: A grant counted in the budget but not yet received is a cash timing exposure that a finance director would need to track against spending.
findings.figures: £900k MHCLG grant; original budget £21.3 million; total budget £22.2 million
findings.quote: £900k MHCLG Section 31 grant funding which has been incorporated into the revised budget, albeit not yet received.

findings.committee: Joint Scrutiny Panel - Local Government Reorganisation
findings.headline: Budget includes £4.033 million for redundancy costs but no provision for pension strain costs.
findings.detail: The paper describes pension strain as a significant area of uncertainty and lists it as one of the most significant financial risks. It remains unquantified in the budget.
findings.matters: Pension strain on a reorganisation is often a large, unbudgeted cost, and other councils going through LGR would want to know it is outside the envelope here.
findings.figures: £4.033 million redundancy budget; Redundancy £4,033,000 in Appendix B
findings.quote: The budget includes £4.033 million for redundancy costs but does not include pension strain costs, which remain a significant area of uncertainty.

findings.committee: Joint Scrutiny Panel - Local Government Reorganisation
findings.headline: ICT transition budget of £2.8 million is expected to be insufficient and to need virement from other budget lines.
findings.detail: Detailed implementation planning is still underway, and costs for ERP, data migration, cyber security and infrastructure remain subject to refinement. The paper states that the budget will not be sufficient and will require virement, so the overspend will be met from other programme lines.
findings.matters: A forecast shortfall that must be covered by moving money between budget lines is a risk to the overall envelope that a finance director would want to track.
findings.figures: £2.8 million ICT transition budget; ICT Transition Costs £2,800,000 in Appendix B
findings.quote: This budget will not be sufficient and will require virement from other budget lines.

daily_post.lead: Ringfenced grant that replaces core-funded spend is a common way councils manage homelessness costs, and the report links it to a deferral of future commitments.
